A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of the GENIUS paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GENIUS retrieval experiments on M-BEIR, Flickr30K and COCO, together with component ablations, efficiency measurements and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original retrieval experiments, ablations and analyses, with two revised numerical entries in Table 2.

M1.justification: The encoder, fusion module, residual quantizer, losses, query interpolation, decoder and inference procedures are unchanged. Figure 2 revisions clarify the existing prefix-embedding representation rather than introducing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten M-BEIR datasets and eight retrieval tasks, alongside the same Flickr30K and COCO evaluations. Task-specific, universal and zero-shot scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same CLIP/BLIP variants, GRACE, IRGen and appendix GRACE identifier variants. Newly cited residual-quantization papers are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, retrieval pools, recall metrics, training budgets, model configurations and beam settings remain unchanged in Section 5 and the appendices. No protocol revision accompanies the changed Table 2 values.

E4.justification: The component ablations, codebook configurations, modality-encoding comparisons, beam and decoder sensitivity studies, UMAP analysis and hierarchical-code examples are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: In Table 2, GENIUS's FashionIQ Recall@10 changes from 18.9 to 13.1, and its reported average changes from 28.8 to 27.6. Appendix Table 14 retains 18.9 and 28.8 for GENIUS with 50 beams. Other reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, quantization equations and training objectives are unchanged. Explicit R^d annotations for fused embeddings clarify existing dimensions; they introduce no new mathematical definition, assumption or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about universal generative retrieval, modality-decoupled quantization, query augmentation, retrieval efficiency and performance relative to existing methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality separation, contrastive alignment, augmentation and efficiency tradeoffs are unchanged, as is the limitation on knowledge-intensive retrieval. No new discussion explains the Table 2 revisions.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains unchanged, including Section 5.2 hyperparameters and Appendix B.2 hardware and training times. The added dimensional annotations do not disclose a different architecture or configuration.

R1.justification: V2 adds three references: Lee et al.'s residual-quantization image generation, Rajput et al.'s generative retrieval for recommender systems, and Zeghidour et al.'s SoundStream. These improve attribution in Sections 2.2 and 4.2 without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited notation, citation and version-header edits, notably explicit R^d membership in Section 4.2.1. The narrative, section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adjusts mathematical labels and redraws prefix embeddings as stacked arrays. Minor text and bibliography reflow also occurs. No figures or tables are added or removed, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Citation additions and Figure 2 refinements improve attribution and clarity, but numerical consistency worsens. V1's Table 2 FashionIQ score and GENIUS average agreed with Appendix Table 14; v2 changes them without updating the appendix. Moreover, v2's displayed GENIUS scores average approximately 28.4, rather than the reported 27.6. These unexplained discrepancies weaken result reporting and outweigh the limited presentation gains.
